So, how do you put together an effective evaluation process? Broadly
speaking, you can think of the evaluation process in four parts.

First, you analyze what the agent should do and how
it actually behaves.

You look for situations where it might fail and use error analysis to
identify and group the failures you observe.

Second, you use what you've learned to build and refine a
reusable set of test cases,

Third, you use evaluators to judge the results and measure how
well the agent performs.

And fourth, you use those findings to make changes,
then test again to see what improved and whether anything got worse.
